metadata.title: Stock Market Today: Futures Rise After Losing Day for S&P 500, Nasdaq; Oil Prices Pull Back; Bitcoin Tops $80K

content.text:
Stock Market Today: Futures Rise After Losing Day for S&P 500, Nasdaq; Oil Prices Pull Back; Bitcoin Tops $80K
Stock futures pointed to a higher open Tuesday, a day after the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 began the week with losses, as oil prices retreated and bitcoin topped $80,000 for the first time in more than three months.
Nasdaq 100, S&P 500, and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 1%, 0.5%, and 0.5%, respectively, in recent trading.
Yesterday, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite started the week lower as semiconductor stocks dropped, while the blue-chip Dow ended higher for a second straight session.
The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM), which sank nearly 6% Monday, was up 3.5% before the bell as components Sandisk (SNDK), Western Digital (WDC), SK Hynix (SKHY), Micron Technology (MU), and Seagate Technology (STX) rebounded. The broader iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) was 2.5% higher after declining more than 2.5% yesterday, aided by a rebound from components Marvell Technology (MRVL), Intel (INTC), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Applied Materials (AMAT).
Nvidia (NVDA), another component of the iShares Semiconductor ETF, pointed up about 1.5% after closing nearly 3% lower yesterday—its seventh straight decline, marking its longest skid since 2022. The world's most valuable public company is set to report highly anticipated quarterly results Wednesday afternoon. Its fellow Magnificent Seven mega-cap tech stocks were mostly higher before the bell, with Tesla (TSLA) rebounding nearly 1% after ending almost 4% lower yesterday.
Meanwhile, crude oil prices fell further a day after investors shrugged off the Treasury Department's new sanctions on Iran and those that trade with the Middle East nation. West Texas Intermediate futures, the U.S. benchmark, were down 3% at $82.45 a barrel, while Brent crude futures, the global benchmark, were 2.9% lower at $89.55.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury, which influences interest rates on a variety of consumer loans including mortgages, was around 4.67%, down three basis points from Monday's close.
Bitcoin topped the $80,000 threshold for the first time since May 15 early Tuesday. The world's largest cryptocurrency reached as high as $81,222 and recently was trading around $79,300, up slightly over the past 24 hours.
The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the value of the greenback against a basket of foreign currencies, was flat at 99.00. Gold futures slipped 0.2% to $4,690 an ounce but remain near their highest price since mid-May.
In addition to Nvidia's highly anticipated results tomorrow, investors will be paying attention to the July Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index data. The cost-of-living index rose 3.7% year-over-year in June, down from 4.1% in May, and while other inflation trackers also show inflation has cooled, the PCE is the Federal Reserve's preferred gauge.
AUGUST 25, 2026 AT 10:34 AM GMT
Stock Futures Rise After Losing Day for S&P 500, Nasdaq
Futures contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were up 0.5%.
S&P 500 futures also pointed up 0.5%.
Nasdaq 100 futures rose 1%.
